chapter: The Famous Door, Billy May and the Palomar fire
title: The six arrangements Basie gave them, including Moonlight Serenade
summary: Basie gave six pop arrangements, some by Skippy Martin, including a Moonlight Serenade far from Glenn Miller's.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Do you remember what specific numbers Basie gave you?

Yeah. "Moonlight Serenade", was one of them. Actually he gave us six arrangements that he thought that we could use, because see he knew that we had a lot of jazz head arrangements and everything. We were all right in that department. He gave us, "Moonlight Serenade." I can't remember the others, but they were pop tunes. You know. None with vocals, but they were ballads, you know, done very nicely, and --
Arranged by whom? Do you remember?
Well, actually by -- some of them were done by a guy that was playing in our band, Skippy Martin.

He had written quite a bit for the Basie Band back in New York. And I don't know who made the others. I know that Skippy made a couple of them. But they came in quite handy when we regrouped, you know, and -- of course the "Moonlight Serenade" was a far cry from the Glenn Miller version.
